title: Face with Tongue Emoji 😛 Meaning: Teasing and Being Silly
description: The face with tongue emoji 😛 sticks its tongue out to tease, joke or act silly, the emoji form of :P. See when it's playful, when it's flirty, and when it's bratty.
summary: The 😛 face with tongue shows a smiling face with its tongue sticking out. It means the sender is teasing, joking, or being silly, like the old :P emoticon. It softens cheeky remarks, marks playful defiance, and can be mildly flirtatious. Occasionally it carries a suggestive meaning.
meaning: Children stick out their tongues to say “nyah nyah,” and adults typed :P for years to capture the same spirit. 😛 is that emoticon as an emoji. Its main job is to label a remark as playful. “I'm clearly the better cook 😛” is a tease, not a boast, and the tongue makes sure it lands that way.

It is useful for softening. A blunt joke, a bit of friendly mockery, or a small refusal can sting in plain text. Adding 😛 tells the reader no harm is meant. The same goes for self-directed humor: “I may have slept until noon 😛” admits something minor with a grin instead of an apology.

Of the three tongue-out faces, this is the calmest. Its eyes are open and ordinary, with no wink and no squint, so it comes across as lightly cheeky where the others are zany. That makes it a reasonable default when you want to tease someone without seeming hyper. It suits small jokes in the middle of an otherwise normal conversation, where a wilder face would be more than the moment calls for.

In flirting, 😛 keeps things light and a bit bratty, a way of poking at someone you like. There is also a sexual reading, since a protruding tongue can allude to licking or oral sex. That meaning shows up mainly when the message is already suggestive or the emoji is paired with others that point that way. In ordinary conversation, people read it as innocent silliness.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: A regular feature of banter. It follows jabs between friends, siblings, and partners and keeps them friendly. It also answers a tease in kind: when someone ribs you, a lone 😛 says “very funny” without conceding. It tends to feel a little old-school, favored by people who grew up typing :P.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: A sign they are comfortable joking with you, which is often how flirting starts. Teasing plus 😛 suggests playful interest. It is not a strong signal on its own. If the message itself is suggestive, the emoji may be reinforcing that, so read the two together.

contexts.label: In gaming and online chat
contexts.body: Used after beating a friend, dodging a question, or making an obvious joke in chat. It carries the tone of the classic :P from forums and messengers, and plenty of users still type the characters instead. Either form says “don't take this seriously.”

examples.text: You're just jealous of my dance moves 😛

examples.meaning: Cheerfully refusing to share a secret.

examples.text: I ate your leftovers. Sorry not sorry 😛
examples.meaning: Cheeky confession with no real remorse.

examples.text: Oops, forgot to set an alarm again 😛
examples.meaning: Laughing off a small personal failing.

combos.meaning: Extra teasing; rubbing it in a little.
Goofy, carefree mood, often in a selfie caption.
A sexually suggestive pairing; not for casual use.
Full silliness; the sender is in a daft mood.

confusedWith.difference: 😜 adds a wink and, on many platforms, uneven eyes. It is wackier and says “I'm kidding around.” 😛 has both eyes open and is a simpler tease. 😜 is the more popular of the two for jokes.
😝 scrunches its eyes shut while sticking out its tongue. It is more intense: gleeful mischief, or sometimes playful disgust. 😛 is relaxed by comparison, a light poke instead of a full raspberry.
😋 has smiling eyes and its tongue curled at the corner of a closed mouth, meaning “yum.” 😛 has an open mouth with the tongue hanging straight down, meaning teasing. Use 😋 for food and 😛 for jokes.

avoid: Don't use it in professional messages except with colleagues you joke with regularly.
Avoid it after real criticism, where sticking out your tongue looks childish or dismissive.
Be careful sending it with suggestive wording to someone who may not welcome that.
design: A yellow face with open oval eyes and a smiling open mouth, from which a pink or red tongue extends downward. No wink, squint, or blush. Apple, Google, Samsung, and Microsoft show the same basic face, with the tongue's length and color varying a little. It is the plainest of the tongue-out smileys.

faqs.a: Yes. :P is the text emoticon for sticking out your tongue, and 😛 is its emoji counterpart. Many apps convert the typed characters into this face or one of its close relatives automatically.

It can be part of flirting, because teasing often is. By itself it mostly means playfulness. Between people who are already flirting, it adds a cheeky, challenging note. Between friends, it is simply a joke marker.

faqs.q: What does 😛 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: They are teasing you or being silly. That shows comfort and good humor. If their words are suggestive, the emoji may underline it. Otherwise assume innocent fun, regardless of the sender's gender.

Sometimes. A stuck-out tongue can hint at licking, and in an explicitly sexual conversation or combined with emojis like 💦 it is read that way. In everyday chat it is not sexual, and most uses are harmless.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 😛, 😜 and 😝?
faqs.a: All stick out a tongue. 😛 has plain open eyes and is a mild tease. 😜 winks and is zany. 😝 squeezes its eyes shut and is the most exuberant. Pick by how silly you want to sound.
